name: Drag and Drop

hero.title: A sortable list in one hook. Keyboard users included.
hero.lede: Reorder lists, build kanban boards and take file drops on Atlassian's pragmatic-drag-and-drop. Space picks an item up, the arrows move it, a screen reader hears every step, and every drag state is a signal your JSX reads directly.

facts.value: pragmatic-drag-and-drop<small>Atlassian's engine: native drag events, hit-testing, edges.</small>
Space · arrows · Esc<small>Alt+Arrow moves directly. Each step is announced.</small>
{dot:ok} sortable, draggable, droppable<small>Experimental. SwiftUI `.onDrag`/`.onDrop`, Compose drag-and-drop. File drop and the monitor stay web.</small>

proof.label: faster hover across 1,000 rows: `isOverKey` wakes the two rows involved, a hand-written `overId() === key` wakes every row
proof.source: BENCHMARKS.md §10, dnd row · overnight run, one run, bun, happy-dom (relative only)

why.title: The parts of drag and drop nobody finishes.

items.title: Keyboard reordering, on by default
items.text: Focus a row, Space or Enter picks it up, the arrows move it, Space drops it and Escape puts it back. Alt+Arrow moves in one step. No sensors to configure.

items.title: Screen readers hear every move
items.text: "Picked up Fix Safari bug. Current position 4 of 4." then "Moved Fix Safari bug to position 3 of 4." Items get `aria-roledescription`, plus `role="listitem"` and keyboard instructions unless you set your own.

items.title: State you read, not render props
items.text: `activeId()`, `overId()` and `overEdge()` are signals, and `isOverKey(id)` answers per row. A drop indicator is `class={() => s.isOverKey(t.id) ? s.overEdge() : ''}`: when the hover moves, only the row it left and the row it entered update.

items.title: Files with reasons
items.text: `useFileDrop({ accept: ['image/*'], maxFiles: 5 })` gives you the accepted files, and `onReject(files, 'accept' | 'maxFiles')` tells you why the rest were refused.

difference.title: Delete the sensors, the contexts and `arrayMove`.

before.label: React + dnd-kit
before.caption: Two providers, two sensors, a per-row hook with a style transform, and the reorder written by hand.

after.label: with @pyreon/dnd
after.caption: One hook. Pointer, keyboard, announcements and auto-scroll included; you get the reordered array.

items.name: `useSortable`
items.text: Reorder with edge detection and auto-scroll; `axis: 'horizontal'` for rows of cards.

items.name: Boards
items.text: `groupId` links lists, `onCrossListDrop` and `onCrossListReceive(item, index)` move cards between them.

items.name: `itemHandleRef`
items.text: Drag only by the grip, keep the rest of the row clickable.

items.name: `useDroppable`
items.text: `canDrop(source)` filters, `edges` turns on `overEdge()` for which side you are on, `isOver()` lights the target.

items.name: `useFileDrop`
items.text: Real OS files only, with `accept`, `maxFiles` and `isDraggingFiles()` for a page-wide hint.

items.name: `useDragMonitor`
items.text: Watch every element drag on the page, with `canMonitor` to filter, for an overlay or analytics.

items.name: Keyboard and live region
items.text: Pick up, move, drop and cancel with announcements through `@pyreon/a11y`.

items.name: `disabled`
items.text: A boolean or a signal: lock a list while it saves.

items.name: Cleanup by design
items.text: Every engine registration is torn down on unmount, and per item when its ref goes `null`.

recipes.title: A drop indicator that touches two rows, not all of them
recipes.text: `isOverKey(id)` and `overEdge()` are signals. The line appears above or below the hovered card, and a hover move updates only the row it left and the row it entered.

recipes.title: An avatar drop zone that says no politely
recipes.text: One image at a time. Rejections come with a reason you can show.

limits.title: Give `items` as a signal or getter
limits.text: `useSortable` reads `items()` when a drop lands. A captured array goes stale after the first reorder.

limits.title: Match `by` with `<For by>`
limits.text: Use the same key in the hook's `by`, in `itemRef(key)` and in `<For by>`: the hook finds the dragged row by that key, and `<For>` moves the existing DOM node instead of rebuilding it.

limits.title: File drop is for OS files
limits.text: `useFileDrop` reacts to files dragged in from the desktop, not to in-app drags. Use `useDroppable` for those.

limits.title: On native, the gesture hooks only
limits.text: iOS and Android lower `useSortable`, `useDraggable` and `useDroppable` to the platform drag engines. The page-wide monitor and OS file drop stay web. Native targets are experimental.

faq.q: Is it accessible without extra work?
faq.a: Sortable lists are. Items become focusable with list semantics and instructions, the keyboard flow is built in, and every pick-up, move, drop and cancel is announced. `label(item)` makes the announcement say "Fix Safari bug" instead of an id.

It is built on the browser's native drag events, which is also what lets files arrive from the desktop, and it is the engine behind Trello and Jira. `@pyreon/dnd` adapts its state into signals and its teardown into `onCleanup`.

Against a hand-rolled signals + pragmatic-drag-and-drop integration, measured in one run under happy-dom: mount and unmount tie, each drag start and drop adds about 5 ns, registering a page monitor about 82 ns, and a hover move across 1,000 rows is 20× cheaper with `isOverKey` than with a per-row `overId() === key`. happy-dom times are relative, not browser times.

faq.q: How do I build a kanban board?
faq.a: One `useSortable` per column with the same `groupId`. Reordering inside a column calls `onReorder`; a card dropped into another column calls `onCrossListDrop(item)` on the source and `onCrossListReceive(item, index)` on the target, where you move it between your signals.

benchmarks.rival: vs a hand-rolled signals + raw pragmatic-drag-and-drop integration · bun, happy-dom
benchmarks.run: overnight run, one run, happy-dom: relative only
benchmarks.p: The baseline is what you would write without the wrapper: the same engine calls, the same signals, the same cleanup. Mounting costs the same, each event and each page monitor adds a few nanoseconds, and a hover that moves across a long list is where the hooks pull ahead. happy-dom is a JavaScript DOM, so read the ratios, not the times.
